values: Fictional materials: one round of organic and paid search campaigns
M1｜A completely fictional software product and two search channels. Do not use real query logs, personal identities, advertising accounts or client budgets.
M2｜Organic search showed 10,000 impressions, 300 clicks and 30 recorded conversions in the same observation week; assume the click and conversion event definitions are consistent.
M3｜Paid search showed 5,000 impressions, 200 clicks and 20 recorded conversions in the same period, with a spend of 800 USD.
M4｜The pre-set paid campaign CPA target is no higher than 35 USD. CTR, post-click conversion rate and CPA must be calculated, then judged against the target.

M5｜Also run a fictional landing page A/B test: group A had 100 clicks and 8 conversions; group B had 100 clicks and 12 conversions. The proportional difference can be calculated, but a small sample cannot directly establish real incremental gain.

M6｜In the second week of implementation someone changed the conversion event tag, and whether it fires twice is not yet verified; the campaign review should first pause definitive conclusions and ask the analytics owner to verify the event and attribution.

Organic CTR=300/10,000=3%, post-click conversion rate=30/300=10%; paid CTR=200/5,000=4%, post-click conversion rate=20/200=10%.

Group A conversion rate 8/100=8% and group B 12/100=12%, an apparent difference of 4 percentage points; the sample is small and M6 tracking is unverified, so causation cannot be claimed and volume should not be scaled up directly.
